correctness.rationale: The positive polynomial ideal and its tail above n are stable for the stated product and it inherits both Novikov identities. Homogeneous components of an arbitrary derivation are derivations. The right identity and left diagonal action of e₁ yield (s+1)c₁=0 and scⱼ=−jc₁ for active indices at shift s. Off the zero residue the only direction has s≡−1 and cⱼ proportional to j; at the zero residue, for characteristic ≠2, multiplication by e₂ gives cᵢ₊₁=cᵢ+c₂. At a negative shift divisible by odd p the first active coefficient is killed by the equation at e₋ₛ∘e₂, then all are killed by recurrence. Direct substitution gives discrepancies proportional to s or s+1 for the nonnegative-shift generators; truncation introduces no new condition because a nonnegative shift cannot lower an out-of-range output. Counting gives one direction in characteristic 0 and 1+floor(n/p)+floor((n−2)/p) for odd p. In characteristic 2 the right annihilator B is preserved, and the split product forces an ordinary derivation δ of A, an A-linear map A→B, and a δ-connection on B. The kernel (u^b) must be δ-stable. The two maps contribute 2b free parameters, and the allowed δ(u) has a constant term exactly when both lengths equal an even integer, accounting for the unique shift −2. The two characteristic-two formulas agree; the finite-field count is the cardinality of this vector space.
